Description: Auto insurance CPI up 11.1% YoY (Feb 2025). Premiums rose 64% from Sept 2020 to Sept 2025, outpacing 25% general inflation. Average full coverage $2,638/year = 3.39% of median household income.
Analysis: CONSISTENT WITH THESIS. Auto insurance inflation dramatically outpacing wages. 64% cumulative creates sustained affordability destruction. Rates moderating in 2026 (5.9% Feb 2026) but from massively elevated base.
Data Quote: 11.1% YoY Feb 2025; 64% cumulative 2020-2025; $2,638 avg; 3.39% of median income
Source: BLS CPI, Bankrate, The Zebra, III
Invalidation Criteria: If premium growth drops below wage growth for 2+ quarters
Notes: Updated: Feb 2026 CPI shows moderation to 5.9% YoY

Description: IRC 2025 study: 15.4% uninsured motorist rate in 2023 (1 in 7 drivers). Combined with underinsured: 33.4% inadequately covered (1 in 3). Up 10pp since 2017. Mississippi highest (28.2%), Maine lowest (5.7%).
Analysis: CRITICAL THESIS VALIDATION. One-third of drivers either uninsured or underinsured = massive protection gap. Exceeds 14% ELEVATED threshold. Rising despite economic recovery = affordability is primary driver.
CARL Relevance: One-third of accidents involve inadequate coverage = catastrophic OOP for at-fault or UM victims
Notes: No updated IRC data yet for 2024/2025; trend likely continued

Description: FL Citizens policies COLLAPSED from 1.4M (Oct 2023 peak) to ~336K (Mar 2026) - down 76%. Depopulation program moved 546K policies to private market in 2025. Citizens rate CUT 2.6% approved.
Analysis: CONTRADICTS CRISIS NARRATIVE FOR FL. Major market reversal — 2022 tort reforms working. 17 new insurers entered. Rate cut signals durability of recovery. POSITIVE for FL consumers. Test = 2026 hurricane season.
Data Quote: ~336K policies Mar 2026 (down from 1.42M peak); -76%; 17 new carriers; 2.6% rate cut
Source: Citizens FL, Axios Miami Mar 2026, FL Voice News Jan 2026
CARL Relevance: FL market stabilization reduces CARL housing stress for this geography
Invalidation Criteria: If Citizens growth resumes to >500K or new carriers exit
Notes: Major positive development; FL consumers benefiting from 2022 reforms

Description: CA FAIR Plan exploded to ~650K+ policies with $700B exposure (Sept 2025) — up from 210K in 2020 (5x). Now LARGEST residual market in US. Jan 2025 LA fires caused $4B loss; $1B assessment passed to all CA insured. 36% rate increase sought. 150K uninsured HH in extreme fire areas.
Analysis: CRISIS CONFIRMED AND DEEPENING FOR CA. FAIR Plan growth = structural private market failure. $4B wildfire loss → $1B assessment → higher premiums for all CA insured (amplifier). Sustainable Insurance Strategy underway but unproven. CA insuring 1 in 5 high-fire homes through FAIR Plan.
Data Quote: 650K+ policies; $700B exposure; 5x growth; $4B wildfire loss; 36% rate hike sought
Source: CA DOI, Fitch, Insurance Business, Insurance Journal Mar 2026
CARL Relevance: Property values at risk if uninsurable; mortgage origination implications for CA
Invalidation Criteria: If 6+ major carriers commit to CA re-entry with actual volume
Notes: 2026: growth decelerating (<4% in final Q) but from massively elevated base

Description: KFF 2025 Survey: Employer family premium $26,993/year (+6%); single $9,325 (+5%). Average deductible $1,886 (+17% since 2020). Third consecutive year of 6%+ increases. Small firm workers face $2,631 avg deductible; 53% face $2,000+.
Analysis: CONSISTENT WITH THESIS. Third straight year of 6%+ premium growth outpaces wages. High deductibles create effective underinsurance — coverage exists on paper but $2,000+ threshold prevents use. 154M Americans rely on employer coverage.
Data Quote: $26,993 family premium; $1,886 avg deductible; +17% deductible since 2020; 6% YoY premium
CARL Relevance: High deductibles = underinsurance = medical debt risk when event occurs
Invalidation Criteria: If premium growth falls below wage growth
Notes: First time in 20 years: 6%+ for 3 consecutive years

Description: ACA enrollment fell 4.9% to 23.1M for 2026 plan year (first decline since ARP subsidies). ACA subsidy cliff activated Jan 1, 2026 — share receiving subsidies dropped from 92% to 87%. Avg monthly premium +57% ($113 → $178). 1.5M enrolled without eligibility (Medicaid concurrent or reconciliation fail).
Analysis: ACA CLIFF LANDED. More severe than projected for first-year impact. 1.2M consumers dropped coverage. Monthly premium shock (+57%) = direct measure of affordability destruction. OBBBA projects 15M+ uninsured over time. Working-age uninsured already 11.5%.
CARL Relevance: Rising uninsured = rising medical debt risk = CARL CC and housing stress
Invalidation Criteria: If Congress restores ARP subsidies before next enrollment
Notes: OBBBA further threat: 15M+ uninsured projected by CBO

Description: Medical debt: 100M+ Americans affected, $195B total burden, $88B in active collections. 62% of bankruptcies touch medical debt. 517K bankruptcies filed in 2024 (+14.2%). CFPB rule to remove medical debt from credit reports vacated Jul 2025.
Analysis: CRITICAL CONSUMER VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED. Medical debt is PRIMARY AMPLIFIER — medical events → credit destruction. Scale larger than previously documented ($195B vs $88B cited earlier). Bankruptcy filings rising +14.2%. No federal credit protection after CFPB rule vacated.
Data Quote: 100M Americans; $195B total; $88B collections; 62% of bankruptcies; CFPB rule vacated Jul 2025
CARL Relevance: Medical debt directly damages credit scores; CARL CC DQ connection; medical = leading bankruptcy cause
Invalidation Criteria: If federal protection restored or medical debt forgiven at scale
Notes: $195B total is updated figure vs $88B collections-only; both valid measures

Description: P&C industry combined ratio: 97% in 2024 (best in decade); Auto 2025 CR: Allstate 85.0, Progressive ~88, GEICO ~87 (all profitable). Homeowners line CR 106.1% (unprofitable). Industry overall profitable but HO stressed.
Analysis: BIFURCATED INDUSTRY. Auto returned to strong profitability after 2022-24 losses — rate stabilization likely. HO line unprofitable (106.1%) = continued rate increases and potential exits. This is FORWARD PRESSURE on HO premiums despite auto relief.
Data Quote: 2025 auto: Allstate 85.0 CR, PGR ~88 CR; HO line 106.1% CR; Industry ~97-99%
Source: S&P Global, AM Best, Allstate Q4 2025, PGR Q4 2025 earnings
Thesis Impact: MIXED - industry healthy but HO stress continues
CARL Relevance: HO unprofitability = continued premium pressure on consumers; auto stabilization = modest relief
Invalidation Criteria: If HO combined ratio drops below 100% sustained
Notes: CA wildfire losses will keep HO line under pressure through 2026+

Description: Auto insurance CPI moderated to 5.9% YoY as of Feb 2026, down from 11.1% (Feb 2025) and 19.8% peak (Jun 2023). Allstate/Progressive both reporting excellent profitability. Rate environment stabilizing.
Analysis: MODERATING BUT NOT RESTORED. 5.9% still above historical 3-4% avg. 64% cumulative increase from 2020 base means affordability remains destroyed for bottom 40% even if YoY moderates. Moderate rate increases continuing for safe drivers.
Data Quote: 5.9% YoY Feb 2026; 64% cumulative since 2020; Allstate CR 85.0; PGR CR ~88
Source: BLS CPI Feb 2026, Allstate/PGR Q4 2025 earnings
CARL Relevance: Premium moderation = slight consumer relief but from destructive base; doesn't restore affordability
Invalidation Criteria: If YoY drops to <3% for 3+ consecutive months
Notes: Carriers profitable = less incentive for further rate hikes; but cumulative burden persists

Description: OBBBA (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) signed Jul 4, 2025. CBO projects 11.8M losing Medicaid + 3.1M marketplace = 15M total uninsured by 2034. 2026 implementation: states must conduct Medicaid redeterminations every 6 months (vs annual). Urban Institute: 3 in 10 young adults (18-24) on Medicaid at risk.
Analysis: LARGEST SINGLE COVERAGE THREAT SINCE ACA PASSAGE. Structural policy change creating sustained uninsured pipeline. Six-month redetermination = churn machine; eligible beneficiaries lose coverage through paperwork failure. This is SLOW-MOTION ACA CLIFF on the Medicaid side.
Source: CBO score of OBBBA; Urban Institute Jul 2025; Harvard Chan Aug 2025
CARL Relevance: Rising uninsured → rising medical debt → CARL CC DQ deterioration
Invalidation Criteria: If courts strike down OBBBA provisions or Congress restores Medicaid funding
Notes: First OBBBA implementation effects expected H2 2026

Description: Homeowners premiums projected +4% nationally in 2026 (5th straight increase). CA projected +16% (highest in nation). Average national premium $3,057. FL average ~$8,500 (2.8x national), though rates cut at Citizens.
Analysis: NATIONAL STABLE-ELEVATED; CA ACCELERATING. CA 16% increase driven by LA wildfire aftermath — State Farm emergency rate increase approved in 2025; further increases pending. National +4% = 5th consecutive year = compound effect on affordability.
Data Quote: National +4% proj; CA +16% proj; avg national $3,057; FL avg ~$8,500; CA rates: Nebraska +13%, NM +11%
Source: Insurify Mar 2026, Bankrate Apr 2026, ConsumerAffairs Mar 2026
CARL Relevance: HO premium increases reduce discretionary income; affordability crisis in CA
Notes: CA +16% is wildfire aftermath premium; structural not temporary
